title: Attributing Team Rewards and Scaling Measurement Noise
subtitle: Swarm training · Noise scaling · Mamba-2 / SSD
intro: Two main reads cover a new multi-agent training tutorial with reproduction results and a journal extension of measurement-noise scaling. A brief examines Lao distillation with Thai retention. The classic derives Mamba-2 state-space duality.
window: November 24–27, 2026 (America/New_York; emphasis on updates since the previous issue, with a 72-hour overlap)

articles.paper: Swarms, Flocks, Gangs: How to build, train, and evaluate multi-agent systems
articles.title: New tutorial: a shared policy learns to pool private information
articles.dateNote: Blog: November 26, 2026; underlying paper is older; tutorial and reproduction results
articles.evidence: Read task, training and evaluation settings

blocks.text: Four Qwen3-0.6B agents each see one private integer; any correct complete sorted list wins. The paper was covered November 9; this is a new tutorial with preserved 75-update results. [1] [2]

blocks.label: Reward is specified in the post; the advantage formula summarizes its normalization rule across eight attempts per problem. All four agents share it. C counts generated team tokens; this is not causal credit assignment.

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Private information prevents a valid matched-budget single-agent comparison. Training-token savings do not establish held-out efficiency. The original uses 1+7 H200s; the two-GPU, 50-update walkthrough differs. [1]

articles.paper: A measurement noise scaling law for cellular representation learning
articles.authors: Gokul Gowri · Igor Sadalski · Dan Raviv · Peng Yin · Jonathan Rosenfeld · Allon M. Klein
articles.title: Journal extension: measurement quality beyond sample count
articles.dateNote: Journal: November 26, 2026; preprint first posted March 4, 2025; compared v2: February 20, 2026
articles.evidence: Read relevant journal text and compared prior version

blocks.text: Auxiliary mutual information I(Y;Z) measures task-relevant information. Relative to February v2, the journal adds STATE and simulated correlated-noise/batch-effect analyses. The logarithmic law itself is older. [3] [4]

blocks.tex: X=Y+U,\quad Z=\sqrt\eta X+E,\qquad Y\sim\mathcal N(\mu_Y,\sigma_Y^2),\ U\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_U^2),\ E\sim\mathcal N(0,1)
blocks.label: Paper’s independent scalar Gaussian explanatory model. U is variation unrelated to Y; E is channel noise. η corresponds to SNR after normalization, not raw sequencing depth.
Identity for the Gaussian model; a finite ceiling requires σᵤ²>0. The curve shape in high-dimensional non-Gaussian data is empirical, not a theorem for arbitrary neural networks.

blocks.text: Noise robustness and the high-SNR ceiling remain distinct. More samples need not substitute for better measurements; optimal budget allocation still requires a cost model. [3]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: MI depends on the auxiliary task and estimator. The Gaussian derivation is neither a biological mechanism nor a universal representation-quality metric. No reproduction was performed. [3]

articles.paper: Distilling Kimi-K3.1-Pro into Qwen3.8-27B: Teaching a model a new language
articles.title: Monitor nearby capabilities while distilling a language
articles.evidence: Read method, data mixture and results

blocks.text: Off-policy text distillation trains Qwen3.8-27B LoRA on 3,834 teacher Lao translations plus 989 Thai translations. On 1,012 FLORES-200 devtest sentences, Lao chrF++ rises 5.5→44.3 (teacher 47.5); Thai on 300 sentences rises 46.7→47.8. Human-Lao-only training reaches 44.7 but collapses Thai to 5.3. Data sources and amounts differ, so this is not a strictly budget-matched causal ablation. [5]

classic.title: Three algorithms for one semiseparable matrix
classic.paper: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality
classic.dateNote: ICML 2024; first posting and read version v1: May 31, 2024
classic.question: At fixed training FLOPs and state memory, how do increasing state dimension N and revisiting shared layers change expressivity, and how could an experiment separate them?

blocks.text: After S4 (2021) and input-dependent Mamba (2023), Dao and Gu (ICML 2024) constrain each head’s transition to a scalar times identity. Recurrence and attention then share one structured matrix. [6]

blocks.tex: S_t=a_tS_{t-1}+b_tx_t^\top,\qquad y_t^\top=c_t^\top S_t,\quad S_t\in\mathbb R^{N\times P},\ b_t,c_t\in\mathbb R^N,\ x_t\in\mathbb R^P
blocks.label: Notation for the paper’s single head: S₀=0 and aₜ is scalar. Coefficients may depend on input; the identities use the same coefficients for that input.
Expanding recurrence gives structured masked attention M=(QKᵀ)⊙L with Qᵢ=cᵢ and Kⱼ=bⱼ. Empty products equal one; there is no softmax.
The semiseparable factorization bounds the rank of blocks crossing a boundary, not the rank of the entire T×T matrix.
Chunk-state identity reorganizing Section 6: local matrix products compute within-block outputs and final states; a cross-chunk scan propagates states; past contributions are added back.

blocks.text: Recurrence, quadratic attention and chunking compute the same operator up to floating-point effects. Chunk size changes hardware efficiency; core speedups do not establish end-to-end training speedups. [6]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Theory and algorithm read; implementation not run. Scalar transitions restrict SSD; arbitrary softmax Transformers are not thereby exactly replaceable by the same finite state. OpenAlex records 2,416 citations. [7]
